newsitem.title: USA: Texas regulators back electric industry reforms.
newsitem.headline: Texas regulators back electric industry reforms.

text.p: The Texas Public Utility Commission on Wednesday called on state legislators to expand retail electric competition statewide during this year's legislative session.
The three-member commission recommended the Texas legislature continue the process of expanding competition, a proposal expected to meet stiff opposition from electric utilities in the state.

The regulators recommended opening the state's electric grid to retail competition while adopting new laws aimed at ensuring electric reliability and consumer rights. The commission also sought authority to determine excess costs to "immediately prevent cost-shifting among customers."
With electric and natural gas utilities in Houston and Dallas set to merge, the commission also asked for expanded authority to review mergers for their impact on competition.
The recommendations cap a year-long review of the state's power market.
